pr_title: tests: kernel: work_queue_api: relax test to eliminate racy checks
pr_body:
We can't control ticks accurately enough to detect the transition
between on a queue and being handled, so relax the checks to make
things pass.

Fixes #29329
pr_comments: The tests pass on nrf boards when checked-out on this PR.

+1 to Maciej.
The tests passes on the mec15xxevb_assy6853 (Microchip) board when checked-out on this PR too.

`INFO    - 1/1 mec15xxevb_assy6853       tests/kernel/workq/work_queue_api/kernel.workqueue.api PASSED (device 56.331s)`

issue_context.title: tests: kernel.workqueue.api tests fail on multiple platforms
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Tests "work_submit_to_multipleq" and "work_resubmit_nowait_to_queue " from "tests/kernel/workq/work_queue_api" fail on nrf platforms (nrf52840dk_nrf52840, nrf52dk_nrf52832 and nrf9160dk_nrf9160)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. go to zephyr dir
2. call `./scripts/sanitycheck --hardware-map map.yml --device-testing -T tests/kernel/workq/work_queue_api/`
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
The tests pass

**Impact**
Not clear

**Logs and console output**

```
 START - test_work_submit_to_multipleq Assertion failed at CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR/src/main.c:277: twork_submit_multipleq: k_delayed_work_pending(&new_work) is false FAIL - test_work_submit_to_multipleq
 ```
and
```
START - test_work_resubmit_nowait_to_queue Assertion failed at CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR/src/main.c:357: twork_resubmit_nowait: k_work_pending(&delayed_work_sleepy.work) is true FAIL - test_work_resubmit_nowait_to_queue 
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04
 - Toolchain Zephyr SDK v0.11.3
 - Zephyr version: zephyr-v2.4.0-685-g7e64fba9ed
comments: does not seem to be nrf specific.
I've extracted the fixes for these that were in #28891 since that's stalled.

review_comments: If this is trying to assume that the the "sleepy" item is definitely going to have executed after 1us in all configurations, then that's a test bug as it's sensitive to tick rate.  You probably want k_sleep(K_TICKS(1)) here instead.

No; the expectation there is that the `k_sleep()` above advanced ticks to the point where the work has been submitted, but the work thread hasn't yet pulled it off the queue and processed it.  So this is just introducing a rescheduling point to allow that to happen.

Whether it's `k_sleep(K_TICKS(1))` or `k_usleep(1)` the first-submitted work item doesn't get processed until either 1 or 2 of these sleeps occur.  The preceding test abuses the API by reaching in and mutating the queue, so it may be that the thread is being caught in different states, one of which requires a second chance to run.
